body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced an Iran Designation Update on November 9, 2026.

Further details regarding the specific entities or individuals designated, and the reasons for their inclusion, are expected to be released by OFAC in associated public statements or regulatory filings.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes New Iran-related Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) implemented new Iran-related designations on November 6, 2026.

These designations aim to counter activities deemed detrimental to U.S. national security and foreign policy interests concerning Iran. The specifics of the designated parties and the nature of their activities are anticipated to be detailed in forthcoming OFAC publications.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Cyber-related and Transnational Criminal Organizations, Issues Cuba Designations and Determination
body: On November 5, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations targeting cyber-related activities and transnational criminal organizations.

Concurrently, OFAC issued new designations related to Cuba, alongside the publication of a Cuba-related determination. These actions underscore the U.S. government's commitment to combating illicit activities across various fronts, including cybercrime and support for sanctioned regimes.

articles.headline: OFAC Implements Iran-related Designations, Updates Listings, Issues Alert, and Amends Venezuela GL
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations on November 4, 2026, alongside updates to existing Iran-related listings.

In a comprehensive action, OFAC also published an Iran-related alert and issued an amended Venezuela-related General License, accompanied by a new Frequently Asked Question. These measures reflect ongoing efforts to address illicit activities linked to both Iran and Venezuela.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Amended Iran-related General License
body: On October 29, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued an amended Iran-related General License.
This amendment modifies existing authorizations concerning transactions involving Iran, and parties engaging in Iran-related activities should review the updated guidance to ensure compliance.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Entities Related to North Korea and Democratic Republic of the Congo
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations on October 28, 2026, targeting entities connected to North Korea and the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
These actions aim to disrupt illicit financial networks and activities that support these regimes, reinforcing international efforts to promote peace and stability.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends FAQs on Blocking, Rejecting Transactions, and Filing Reports
body: On October 26, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued amended Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) regarding blocking and rejecting transactions and filing reports with OFAC.
These updates provide further clarification and guidance for financial institutions and other entities on their compliance obligations under OFAC regulations.

articles.headline: OFAC Implements Iran-related Designations, Removes Belarus and North Korea Designations, and Issues New GLs and FAQs
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations on October 21, 2026.

Concurrently, OFAC removed certain designations related to Belarus and North Korea, and issued new General Licenses pertaining to Iran and Russia, along with amended Frequently Asked Questions. These actions reflect a dynamic approach to sanctions policy, adapting to evolving geopolitical landscapes.

articles.headline: OFAC Implements PAIPA Designations and Issues Associated General Licenses
body: On October 19, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) implemented new designations under the Protecting American Intellectual Property Act of 2022 (PAIPA).

These designations are accompanied by the issuance of associated General Licenses, providing guidance on authorized activities. This action underscores the U.S. government's commitment to protecting American intellectual property globally.

articles.headline: BIS Extends Suspension of 'Affiliates Rule' for Entity List Enforcement
body: The U.S. Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) has extended the suspension of its 'Affiliates Rule' until January 10, 2027.

This rule, initially adopted in September 2025, would expand export control restrictions under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) to foreign companies that are 50% or more owned or controlled by parties on the BIS Entity List or Military End-User List.

The suspension, which was previously in effect until November 9, 2026, is part of an ongoing U.S.-China trade truce and provides temporary relief for exporters who would otherwise face increased due diligence requirements.
articles.source: Federal Register / Export Compliance Daily / ABA Banking Journal

articles.headline: Department of Commerce Streamlines Export Controls for Sound Suppressors
body: The Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) announced that, as of November 20, 2026, the export of certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors will be subject to BIS's Export Administration Regulations (EAR), rather than the State Department's U.S. Munitions List.
This deregulatory action aims to align export controls on suppressors with those already applied to firearms, reducing compliance burdens on the firearms industry while maintaining national security.

Under this new rule, suppressors will be added to the Commerce Control List (CCL), and a license will be required for certain exports, reexports, or in-country transfers, with existing license exceptions for firearms also applicable to suppressors.

articles.headline: DHS Adds 43 Chinese Companies to UFLPA Entity List
body: The U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), chair of the Forced Labor Enforcement Task Force (FLETF), added 43 Chinese companies to the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act (UFLPA) Entity List.
This is the largest single expansion of the UFLPA Entity List since its enactment in 2021, bringing the total number of listed entities to 187.

The newly listed entities are connected to the production and sale of goods made in Xinjiang or with the forced labor of Uyghurs and other ethnic minorities, spanning sectors such as seafood, gold, copper, aluminum, and apparel.
articles.source: U.S. Department of State / Coalition to End Forced Labour in the Uyghur Region / Kharon

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.
